items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: So we brought Teddy... And we’ll put on the trio. And that was the first time that inter-racial anything was ever given in public. And it was the Benny Goodman Trio. And so from there on of course Teddy stayed with the band

ctx.x: It was a concert that Stanley and I had heard. Except the thing was not known in the U.S. you know. And so I went up to talk to Benny, and he’d had a very hard head you know, and only money talked to Benny. And so he listened you know, and he pulled a long face. And I said, “We’re going to put on a concert on Sunday with you.” And he’s thinking you know, what’s the money. And I said, “It’s a benefit for the union, and the union has agreed.” And so well he couldn’t really argue about that. So it was all set. And…
That is — I didn’t know that that had happened like that.
